dedupe_keys.name: northern shenandoah valley publicly funded broadband locations

description: This independent Northern Shenandoah Valley project combines Virginia address points, broadband funding-program locations and public service-qualification checks into one address-level table. The README states 51,080 locations across eight counties and names 2022–2024 Virginia Telecommunication Initiative and BEAD sources. Fields include address and coordinates, funding source, provider lookup result and lookup status. The authors retain unresolved addresses as unknown, not dropping them. The first public release was in September 2026, with a compressed CSV in the GitHub repository. Its own methodology cautions that a provider saying an address is orderable does not prove fibre construction, activation or engineering completion. The licence file has a CC BY 4.0 heading but includes CC0 1.0 legal text, so redistribution terms need clarification. This review read documentation and the file list, not the 10 MB CSV ZIP or individual addresses. A digital-infrastructure modeller could use the status categories to test broadband-access or resilience scenarios, while keeping uncertain matches separate and treating provider checks as observations, not physical-network facts. Related catalogue resource data-fcc-form-477-fixed-broadband-deployment gives older nationwide provider reports, not these funded Virginia locations.
